subject: MAP: concurrency characterization & rate-limit playbook for Q3 close
body:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: concurrency characterization & rate-limit playbook for Q3 close

Hi Samantha / Rajesh —

Per our MAP and the close timeline, attached is the proposed performance benchmarking plan we intend to run on the integration (attached MAP_timeline_v1.xlsx). High level: we need a defined window to run concurrency probes so we can validate TTFT, p50/p95/p99 latencies, steady-state throughput, and burst behavior for the Q3 rollout.

Planned scope (summary):
- Metrics: per-request TTFT, per-token generation latency, p50/p95/p99, tail latencies under concurrency, and failure modes.
- Tests: steady-state ramp to target RPS, fixed-duration bursts (10s/60s/300s), and synthetic unbalanced traffic to trigger queueing/backpressure.
- Concurrency knobs: client-side parallelism, gateway queue size, server token-bucket limits, and batch sizing.
- Acceptance criteria: sustained 200 RPS with p95 < 350ms and p99 < 800ms for steady-state; short bursts up to 500 RPS may be allowed if queueing stays bounded and error rate < 0.5%.
- Deliverables: raw test traces (Gatling CSV), consolidated perf matrix, and a short rate-limit playbook for production (runbook-rate-limit-snippet.txt).

Ask: please confirm the test windows below and whether you'll route synthetic traffic from your staging cluster or want us to generate load from our dedicated harness.
- Proposed windows: 2027-06-02 02:00-06:00 UTC (burst-focused), 2027-06-03 02:00-12:00 UTC (steady-state + longer probes)

I attached the MAP timeline and the initial runbook fragment. If those windows work, we'll lock in the Gatling scenarios and pre-seed API keys.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Performance Engineer (Solutions)

Subject: RE: MAP: initial pilot probes and early findings

Team / Samantha —

Quick update from the pilot we ran against Orion staging on 2027-05-27 using the proposed Gatling scenarios (attached concurrency-gatling-results-20270528.csv). Short summary of what we observed:

Findings:
- Steady-state: with a sustained client-side RPS of ~120 the service hit a comfortable operating point: p95 ~ 220ms, p99 ~ 540ms, error rate < 0.1%. No queueing observed when client RPS <= 140.
- Burst behavior: 60s bursts to 480 RPS caused queueing in the gateway; queue buildup increased end-to-end TTFT and p99 spiked to 1.8s. We observed ~1.2% transient 5xx under the peak burst window (mostly 503/504 from gateway timeouts).
- Long bursts (300s) not executed in this pilot by request — we limited to 60s per Samantha's ask.
- Tokenization: average token-per-request variability affects batch packing; at higher concurrency we saw less effective batching and higher per-token cost.

Preliminary recommendations (for MAP and pre-production runbook):
- Soft rate-limit (token-bucket) at the gateway set to 200 RPS steady with burst capacity 500 tokens and refill interval tuned to 100ms — this keeps steady latencies in target while still permitting short bursts.
- Client backoff guidance: on 429 or 503 return 'Retry-After' guidance starting at 200ms exponential backoff up to 2s.
- Autoscale/awareness: pre-warm model hosts for scheduled high-traffic windows (30–45min lead) to avoid cold-start queueing.
- Observability: capture per-request queue time and batch size; add a dashboard for burst indicators and live queue depth.

Attachments: Gatling CSV + a short runbook snippet with the token-bucket config (runbook-rate-limit-snippet.txt).

Next steps: if the MAP owner approves, we'll bake these into the MAP timeline and run the full steady + burst tests during the secured windows.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor

Thanks for the quick alignment. Per Neha's findings, two operational asks from our side before we run the full MAP tests:

1) Confirmation that Orion will accept a short canary (10% traffic) with the soft rate limit in place on 2027-06-03 02:00-04:00 UTC for validation. Canary would be rolled back automatically if error rate > 0.5% for 5 consecutive minutes.
2) Agreement on an SLA exception to allow controlled brief 503s during the burst probes (we'll provide credits if thresholds are exceeded).

If you approve both, we'll update the MAP timeline and ship the pre-seeded keys + detailed runbook.

-Marissa
